# gron

Make JSON greppable!

gron transforms JSON into discrete assignments to make it easier to `grep` for what you want and see the absolute 'path' to it.
It eases the exploration of APIs that return large blobs of JSON but have terrible documentation.

## Example

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author"
json[0].commit.author = {};
json[0].commit.author.date = "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z";
json[0].commit.author.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json[0].commit.author.name = "Tom Hudson";
```

gron can work backwards too, enabling you to turn your filtered data back into JSON:

```
▶ gron "https://api.github.com/repos/tomnomnom/gron/commits?per_page=1" | fgrep "commit.author" | gron --ungron
[
  {
    "commit": {
      "author": {
        "date": "2016-07-02T10:51:21Z",
        "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
        "name": "Tom Hudson"
      }
    }
  }
]
```

## Usage

Get JSON from a file:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json 
json = {};
json.contact = {};
json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
json.github = "https://github.com/tomnomnom/";
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[1] = "cheese";
json.likes[2] = "meat";
json.name = "Tom";
```

From a URL:

```
▶ gron http://headers.jsontest.com/
json = {};
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "gron/0.1";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "6917a823919477919dbc1523584ba25d/11970839830843610056";
```

Or from `stdin`:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron
json = {};
json.Accept = "*/*";
json.Host = "headers.jsontest.com";
json["User-Agent"] = "curl/7.43.0";
json["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"] = "c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147";
```

Grep for something and easily see the path to it:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep twitter
json.contact.twitter = "@TomNomNom";
```

gron makes diffing JSON easy too:

```
▶ diff <(gron two.json) <(gron two-b.json)
3c3
< json.contact.email = "mail@tomnomnom.com";
---
> json.contact.email = "contact@tomnomnom.com";
```

The output of `gron` is valid JavaScript:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json > tmp.js
▶ echo "console.log(json);" >> tmp.js
▶ nodejs tmp.js
{ contact: { email: 'mail@tomnomnom.com', twitter: '@TomNomNom' },
  github: 'https://github.com/tomnomnom/',
  likes: [ 'code', 'cheese', 'meat' ],
  name: 'Tom' }
```

It's also possible to obtain the `gron` output as JSON stream via the `--json` switch:

```
▶ curl -s http://headers.jsontest.com/ | gron --json
[[],{}]
[["Accept"],"*/*"]
[["Host"],"headers.jsontest.com"]
[["User-Agent"],"curl/7.43.0"]
[["X-Cloud-Trace-Context"],"c70f7bf26661c67d0b9f2cde6f295319/13941186890243645147"]
```

## ungronning

gron can also turn its output back into JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | gron -u
{
  "contact": {
    "email": "mail@tomnomnom.com",
    "twitter": "@TomNomNom"
  },
  "github": "https://github.com/tomnomnom/",
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ],
  "name": "Tom"
}
```

This means you can use gron with `grep` and other tools to modify JSON:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

Or with JSON stream mode:

```
▶ gron --json testdata/two.json | grep likes | gron --json --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    "cheese",
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

To preserve array keys, arrays are padded with `null` when values are missing:

```
▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese
json.likes = [];
json.likes[0] = "code";
json.likes[2] = "meat";

▶ gron testdata/two.json | grep likes | grep -v cheese | gron --ungron
{
  "likes": [
    "code",
    null,
    "meat"
  ]
}
```

## Command-line Options

```
Transform JSON (from a file, URL, or stdin) into discrete assignments to make it greppable

Usage:
  gron [OPTIONS] [FILE|URL|-]

Options:
  -u, --ungron     Reverse the operation (turn assignments back into JSON)
  -v, --values     Print just the values of provided assignments
  -c, --colorize   Colorize output (default on tty)
  -m, --monochrome Monochrome (don't colorize output)
  -s, --stream     Treat each line of input as a separate JSON object
  -k, --insecure   Disable certificate validation
  -j, --json       Represent gron data as JSON stream
      --no-sort    Don't sort output (faster)
      --version    Print version information

Exit Codes:
  0	OK
  1	Failed to open file
  2	Failed to read input
  3	Failed to form statements
  4	Failed to fetch URL
  5	Failed to parse statements
  6	Failed to encode JSON

Examples:
  gron /tmp/apiresponse.json
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 
  curl -s http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | gron
  gron http://jsonplaceholder.typicode.com/users/1 | grep company | gron --ungron
```

## Aliases

It's recommended that you alias `ungron` or `norg` (or both!) to `gron --ungron`:

```bash
alias norg="gron --ungron"
alias ungron="gron --ungron"
```

#!/bin/bash
# Run the reference gron with color enabled (NO_COLOR unset, TERM=xterm), showing exact bytes.
exec env -u NO_COLOR TERM=xterm /workspace/executable "$@"
---
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Run a command with stdout attached to a pty. Usage: ptyrun.py CMD ARGS... [stdin from pipe]"""
import os, pty, sys, subprocess
def run(args, stdin_data=None, env=None):
    m, s = pty.openpty()
    p = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=s, stderr=subprocess.PIPE,
                         stdin=subprocess.PIPE if stdin_data is not None else subprocess.DEVNULL,
                         env=env)
    os.close(s)
    if stdin_data is not None:
        try:
            p.stdin.write(stdin_data)
        except BrokenPipeError:
            pass
        p.stdin.close()
    out = b""
    while True:
        try:
            d = os.read(m, 65536)
        except OSError:
            break
        if not d: break
        out += d
    p.wait()
    os.close(m)
    return out, p.stderr.read(), p.returncode
if __name__ == "__main__":
    env = dict(os.environ); env.pop("NO_COLOR", None); env["TERM"] = "xterm"
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read() if not sys.stdin.isatty() else None
    o, e, r = run(sys.argv[1:], data, env)
    sys.stdout.write("STDOUT: " + repr(o) + "\n")
    if e: sys.stdout.write("STDERR: " + repr(e) + "\n")
    sys.stdout.write("exit=%d\n" % r)
---

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Exhaustive sweep: for a large set of codepoints, determine BARE/quoted in first and
subsequent position, and compare against a hypothesised category rule."""
import subprocess, sys, unicodedata

EXE = "/workspace/executable"

def jesc(cp):
    b = chr(cp).encode('utf-16-be')
    out = b''
    for i in range(0, len(b), 2):
        out += b'\\u%04x' % ((b[i] << 8) | b[i+1])
    return out

def batch(cps, prefix=b''):
    """Return dict cp -> True if bare."""
    res = {}
    CHUNK = 2000
    for i in range(0, len(cps), CHUNK):
        chunk = cps[i:i+CHUNK]
        parts = []
        for n, cp in enumerate(chunk):
            parts.append(b'"' + prefix + jesc(cp) + b'":' + str(n).encode())
        doc = b'{' + b','.join(parts) + b'}'
        p = subprocess.run([EXE], input=doc, capture_output=True)
        if p.returncode != 0:
            print("RC!=0", p.returncode, p.stderr[:200]); sys.exit(1)
        # map index -> bare?
        for ln in p.stdout.split(b'\n'):
            if not ln or ln == b'json = {};':
                continue
            # ln = json<PATH> = <n>;
            assert ln.startswith(b'json') and ln.endswith(b';'), ln
            body = ln[4:-1]
            lhs, _, rhs = body.rpartition(b' = ')
            n = int(rhs)
            cp = chunk[n]
            res[cp] = lhs.startswith(b'.')
    return res

FIRST_CATS = {'Lu','Ll','Lt','Lm','Lo','Nl'}
CONT_CATS  = FIRST_CATS | {'Nd','Mn','Mc','Pc'}

def expect_first(cp):
    return cp in (0x24, 0x5F) or unicodedata.category(chr(cp)) in FIRST_CATS
def expect_cont(cp):
    return cp in (0x24, 0x5F) or unicodedata.category(chr(cp)) in CONT_CATS

# Sweep all of BMP except surrogates + a slice of supplementary planes
cps = [c for c in range(0x20, 0x10000) if not (0xD800 <= c <= 0xDFFF)]
cps += list(range(0x10000, 0x11000)) + list(range(0x1D400, 0x1D800)) \
     + list(range(0x1F300, 0x1F400)) + list(range(0x20000, 0x20100)) \
     + list(range(0xE0000, 0xE0100))
print("sweeping", len(cps), "codepoints")

rf = batch(cps)
rc_ = batch(cps, prefix=b'a')

print("py unicodedata version:", unicodedata.unidata_version)
mismatch_f = [c for c in cps if rf.get(c) != expect_first(c)]
mismatch_c = [c for c in cps if rc_.get(c) != expect_cont(c)]
print("FIRST mismatches vs (L|Nl|$|_):", len(mismatch_f))
for c in mismatch_f[:80]:
    print("  U+%04X %s %s gron_bare=%s expected=%s" % (c, unicodedata.category(chr(c)),
        (unicodedata.name(chr(c),'?')), rf.get(c), expect_first(c)))
print("CONT mismatches vs (L|Nl|Nd|Mn|Mc|Pc|$|_):", len(mismatch_c))
for c in mismatch_c[:80]:
    print("  U+%04X %s %s gron_bare=%s expected=%s" % (c, unicodedata.category(chr(c)),
        (unicodedata.name(chr(c),'?')), rc_.get(c), expect_cont(c)))

# category -> set of observed verdicts
from collections import defaultdict
fv = defaultdict(set); cv = defaultdict(set)
for c in cps:
    cat = unicodedata.category(chr(c))
    fv[cat].add(rf.get(c)); cv[cat].add(rc_.get(c))
print()
print("%-4s %-22s %-22s" % ("cat", "first verdicts", "cont verdicts"))
for cat in sorted(fv):
    print("%-4s %-22s %-22s" % (cat, sorted(map(str,fv[cat])), sorted(map(str,cv[cat]))))

"""For each codepoint, render it inside a bracket-quoted KEY and inside a string VALUE,
and compare the two renderings."""
import subprocess, sys, json
EXE="/workspace/executable"

def jesc(cp):
    b=chr(cp).encode('utf-16-be')
    return b''.join(b'\\u%04x'%((b[i]<<8)|b[i+1]) for i in range(0,len(b),2))

def batch(cps):
    """returns cp -> (key_rendering_bytes, value_rendering_bytes)"""
    res={}
    CH=2000
    for i in range(0,len(cps),CH):
        chunk=cps[i:i+CH]
        parts=[]
        for n,cp in enumerate(chunk):
            e=jesc(cp)
            # key: "!<n>!<char>"  -> forced quoting via '!' ; value: same char
            parts.append(b'"!'+str(n).encode()+b'!'+e+b'":"'+e+b'"')
        doc=b'{'+b','.join(parts)+b'}'
        p=subprocess.run([EXE,'--no-sort'],input=doc,capture_output=True)
        assert p.returncode==0,(p.returncode,p.stderr[:300])
        for ln in p.stdout.split(b'\n'):
            if not ln or ln==b'json = {};': continue
            assert ln.startswith(b'json["!') and ln.endswith(b';'), ln
            body=ln[len(b'json["!'):]
            n_s, _, rest = body.partition(b'!')
            n=int(n_s)
            # rest = <keychars>"] = "<valuechars>";
            assert rest.endswith(b'";'), ln
            keypart, _, valpart = rest[:-2].partition(b'"] = "')
            res[chunk[n]]=(keypart, valpart)
    return res
